title: Record Breaker Jacob Kiplimo Is Ushering in a New Era of Speed
summary: Hear from the elite distance runner on redefining endurance racing and helping to pioneer the next generation of running innovation.
body_markdown:
**Speed is often measured as distance over time. When one thinks of Jacob Kiplimo, they probably think *fast* because of how he’s worked that equation: an Olympic bronze medal running a 10K in 27:43; a world record hitting 57:20 in the half-marathon; a blistering 2:00:28 for the marathon, the third fastest time ever. For Kiplimo, however, speed doesn’t come from seeing the right pixels on a stopwatch. After all, distance over time can’t measure the thousands of miles he's run during his 25 years.**


**Instead, speed is defined by a childhood in rural Uganda trying to keep up with four older brothers. Speed is also defined by friendship through competition with Olympic gold medalist and compatriot Joshua Cheptegei, as each athlete seeks to bring pride to their country by breaking into the upper echelon of African running. Paradoxically, speed for Kiplimo is also defined by the slowness of a farm and the satisfaction of a meal that has been nurtured over months from root to spoon — similar to the quiet work that goes into a long-awaited breakthrough on the course.**


**The at-times bashful Ugandan is likely fast because he also has a confident side, one that keeps him fearless and undeterred by failure. Yes, Kiplimo has had successes and setbacks, but we would not know which is which if we simply looked at race results. If the now-established running star simply measured himself by distance over time, he wouldn’t be able to push the impossible.**


**Here, he speaks in his own words on what it means to compete for his country, the importance of slowing down, and how his partnership with Nike is helping him rewrite the record books.**
